titulo: Why we use a silly voice with our cats (and why it actually works)
trecho: You do it. Everyone does. That high-pitched, drawn-out, slightly ridiculous voice you use only for your cat. Science calls it cat-directed speech — and there are serious studies explaining why it works.

titulo: Why Cats Can't Taste Sweetness: The Genetics Behind Feline Indifference
trecho: Cats are genuinely unable to detect sweet flavors — and the reason is written in their DNA. Learn about the Tas1r2 pseudogene, what it means for feline nutrition, and why sugar still poses real metabolic risks.

titulo: Bombay Cat: The Parlor Panther
trecho: Explore the genetics, behavior and care of the Bombay Cat — the breed engineered to look like a panther and act like a dog.

titulo: What Cats See That You Can't
trecho: Your cat stares at nothing? The explanation isn't supernatural — it's physiology. UV vision, ultrasonic hearing, and dual olfaction create a world invisible to humans.

titulo: Feline Neonatal Isoerythrolysis: the Hidden Danger in Colostrum
trecho: Colostrum exists to protect. In Type B queens mated with Type A males, it can destroy their own kittens. Understand the feline AB blood group system and how to prevent neonatal isoerythrolysis in breeds like Devon Rex and British Shorthair.

titulo: Are Sunflowers Safe for Cats? What Science Says
trecho: Sunflowers (Helianthus annuus) are classified by the ASPCA as non-toxic to cats. But there is a myth about their flowers that most people still believe — plus a comparison with yellow flowers that are actually dangerous.

titulo: Feline Grimace Scale: The 2026 Update Every Cat Owner Needs to Know
trecho: The Feline Grimace Scale was validated for brachycephalic cats in January 2026. Understand what changed, how the scale works, and how any cat owner can use it to identify pain in their cat before it is too late.

titulo: Peterbald: the hairless cat from Saint Petersburg
trecho: Born in 1994 from an experimental cross between a Donskoy and an Oriental Shorthair, the Peterbald carries a dominant hair-loss gene unique in feline genetics. Discover the science, history and care of this extraordinary Russian breed.

titulo: Oscar, the Cat Who Sensed Death
trecho: Oscar was an ordinary cat at a palliative care home — until he predicted over 100 deaths. Science tried to explain it: ketones, warmth, observational learning. No answer is complete.

titulo: Minoxidil and Cats: What You Need to Know
trecho: Minoxidil is popular for hair loss, but it can be dangerous for cats. Understand the chemistry, the real risks, and how to protect your feline without giving up your treatment.

titulo: Are Orchids Safe for Cats? Origin, Care and Safety
trecho: Orchids survived 120 million years and arrived in our homes without posing any danger to cats. Learn about their origin, care requirements, and why the ASPCA classifies them as non-toxic to felines.

titulo: Belly Up: The Science Behind Your Cat's Most Adorable Gesture
trecho: When your cat exposes their belly, they are showing trust — not asking for a rub. Discover the neuroscience and behavior behind this adorable feline gesture and why touching it might be a mistake.
